Given your significant weight loss, I am particularly concerned about malignancy; do you have any known history of pancreatitis or gallstones?

The CT and ultrasound results are surprisingly normal given your severe weight loss and classic cholestatic symptoms, which makes pancreatic cancer unlikely. Have you experienced any fever or chills recently, and could you tell me if you have a history of autoimmune diseases or recent skin rashes?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The imaging and tumor markers have effectively ruled out pancreatic cancer and cholangiocarcinoma, so we must focus on other causes. Given your 40-year history of heavy alcohol use and the recent onset of these symptoms, do you suspect any history of viral hepatitis (like Hepatitis B or C) or have you noticed any easy bruising or bleeding gums?

REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis_Serology; Coagulation_Profile; Ceruloplasmin

DIAGNOSIS READY: Wilson's Disease (unlikely given age) or Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC) / Primary Biliary Cholangitis (PBC) / Cholangiolopathy due to prior alcohol, but the classic presentation of painless jaundice with weight loss and normal CT/Ultrasound in a 72-year-old strongly points toward an occult malignancy not yet visualized (e.g., early ampullary tumor) or a non-obstructive chole
